title: AdicFiniteCompletionBounds
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring and $J$ an ideal. Use constant coefficient sheaves, module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The normalized constructions are [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. For $N$ in the pro-etale derived category put $P_n=A/J^{n+1}$ and $N_n=N\otimes_A^L P_n$, and let $\nu^*$ be the recorded comparison inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Suppose $N$ is locally derived $J$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete] and every $N_n$ has Tor amplitude in one interval $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Then the product of the underlying $A$-complexes exists, $N$ is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] for the actual normalized quotient transitions, and $H^q(N)=0$ when $q<a$ or $b<q$. No etale origin is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes; Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; parent proof steps specified below.

proof.text: Test each reduction Tor bound against the coefficient ring. A flat K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and the tensor-unit isomorphism turn this test into vanishing of its own cohomology outside [a,b]. Exact restriction of scalars from [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data] commutes with cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], so every underlying reduction U_n has the same vanishing. These are the proved private lemmas tor_cohomology_bounds and underlying_cohomology_bounds.

Apply [lem-sfb-adic-finite-completion-tower] to obtain a distinguished derived-limit triangle for completion N with the actual normalized Roos map. Since A is Noetherian, J has finitely many generators. The quotient/Koszul completion-unit criterion [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and the completeness of N make the prescribed completion unit invertible. Compose the first triangle map with this unit, and the final map with its shifted inverse. The explicit triangle isomorphism transports distinguishedness and proves that N is the derived limit of its normalized reductions.

Transport exact countable products [det-pe-products-exact] from the actual pro-etale site to the coefficient-sized model using its site equivalence [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]; model_exact_products proves this transport via the equivalence of module-sheaf categories. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], cohomology preserves the countable product of U_n. Since each H^q(U_n) vanishes outside [a,b], so does H^q(product U_n).

Apply the cohomology long exact sequence of the transported triangle [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. If q is outside [a,b] and q is not b+1, both adjacent product cohomology objects H^(q-1) and H^q vanish, forcing H^q(N)=0. For q=b+1 use [lem-sfb-adic-finite-top-roos-epi] with the residue Tor bound hTor 0: H^b of the Roos map is epic. The successive composite with the connecting morphism is zero, so that connecting morphism is zero. The next product cohomology object also vanishes. Exactness now forces H^(b+1)(N)=0. This proves the second conclusion without a separate Milnor short exact sequence.

lean.statement:
theorem adicFiniteCompletion_bounds
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (N : adicFiniteAmbient.{u, v} X A)
    (hcomplete : adicFiniteComplete.{u, v} X A J N)
    (a b : ℤ)
    (hTor : ∀ n : ℕ, HasCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude.{u, v} X (adicFiniteCoeff J n)
      (adicFiniteReduction.{u, v} X J N n) a b) :
    (∃ hp : HasProduct (adicFiniteUnderlying.{u, v} X J N),
      @IsDerivedLimit _ _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hp (adicFiniteTransition.{u, v} X J N) N) ∧
    (∀ q : ℤ, (q < a ∨ b < q) → IsZero ((coefficientModelCohomology
      (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A) q).obj N))
